concepts.title: Inverted index
concepts.meaning: Term keys connect to ordered posting-list entries for matching documents.
concepts.brief: Connect term entries to ordered posting lists. Show term frequency or position metadata separately from document identifiers, then score candidates with a lexical ranking rule.
pitfalls: An inverted index maps terms to candidate documents; it does not rank semantic relevance by itself.
Posting lists may store frequencies and positions in addition to identifiers.

headings: Sparse retrieval starts with an inverted index

concepts.title: Embedding metric geometry
concepts.meaning: Vector angle and length make different similarity measures visible.
concepts.brief: Show query and candidate vectors. Recompute dot product, cosine similarity, and Euclidean distance, then apply a declared normalization and quantization contract.
pitfalls: Cosine ignores positive magnitude while dot product can depend on it.
Normalization is an explicit serving contract.

headings: Three ways to measure closeness
When the three rulers agree

concepts.title: Grouped query head map
concepts.meaning: Several query heads connect to fewer shared key and value heads.
concepts.brief: Keep all query heads visible while grouping them onto fewer K/V heads. Count cache heads and compare MHA, GQA, and MQA at a fixed head dimension.
pitfalls: GQA reduces K/V heads; it does not remove query heads.
Changing K/V sharing changes the model function and may require uptraining.

concepts.title: Multimodal fusion bridge
concepts.meaning: Image, sound, and text signals enter a shared representation path.
concepts.brief: Follow modality encoders into prefix tokens, side memory, or late fusion while preserving source timestamps and image regions along the shared answer path.
pitfalls: Fusion strategies meet at different model stages.
A pooled similarity vector cannot replace spatial grounding or timestamp evidence.

headings: The concept: one shared evidence path
Fusion strategies

concepts.title: Shared prefix block
concepts.meaning: Two prompt lanes share a complete initial block before their tokens diverge.
concepts.brief: Align prompts token by token, share only compatible full prefix blocks, and allocate private storage after divergence. Include model, adapter, position, and isolation identity.
pitfalls: Matching sentences alone is insufficient when earlier context differs.
A reused prefix saves prompt computation; continuations still read their history.

headings: Two indexes, one causal dependency

concepts.title: Inference latency clocks
concepts.meaning: A long initial processing segment is followed by repeated token intervals.
concepts.brief: Place request, first-token, and later-token timestamps on a timeline. Compute TTFT and inter-token latency, then separate queue, prefill, and decode segments.
pitfalls: Define metric start and end events before reporting.
End-to-end output rate includes initial wait and differs from decode cadence.

headings: Four numbers for one request

concepts.title: Context window budget
concepts.meaning: A finite window is divided among system, history, evidence, request, and output space.
concepts.brief: Allocate finite capacity across instructions, history, evidence, request, and reserved output. Test evidence position without treating a larger window as guaranteed recall.
pitfalls: Input and reserved output share the configured limit.
A prompt can fit yet bury or omit required evidence.

headings: First gate: can the prompt fit, and what does it cost?

concepts.title: Context curation
concepts.meaning: Many source records pass through selection and compression into a focused prompt.
concepts.brief: Start with a large incident record set. Apply selection and compression rules, preserve provenance, and isolate incompatible trust domains before assembling the working context.
pitfalls: Context engineering includes tool definitions and memory, not only retrieved documents.
Compression can remove qualifiers that change a policy meaning.

headings: The four context moves

concepts.title: GPU autoscale pool
concepts.meaning: Queue pressure triggers new GPU replicas that become ready after warmup.
concepts.brief: Track arrivals, queue age, warm replicas, cold-start time, and capacity at each control interval. Scale before the service target is breached and verify replicas before routing traffic.
pitfalls: GPU utilization alone may hide queue growth and latency.
A scheduled replica serves no traffic until its model is loaded and warmed.

headings: A burst needs capacity before its deadline

concepts.title: Local model memory map
concepts.meaning: Model weights and active state occupy separate device and host memory pools.
concepts.brief: Budget weights, K/V state, workspace, and reserve across GPU, unified, and host memory. Show how block offload changes where execution occurs.
pitfalls: CPU offload can change latency and throughput substantially.
Model size alone omits cache, workspace, and allocator overhead.

headings: Build a budget for each memory pool

concepts.title: Agent recovery state
concepts.meaning: A timed-out action is verified before a safe retry or operator handoff.
concepts.brief: Persist one operation key and approved payload before dispatch. After timeout, query the external system with that key; retry only when idempotency and reconciliation rules allow it.
pitfalls: A timeout does not prove a remote write failed.
An idempotent retry must reuse its operation identity.

headings: Lose the reply after a real local commit

concepts.title: Persistent memory tiers
concepts.meaning: Working context can write to and recall from several durable memory layers.
concepts.brief: Separate current working context from durable sourced memories. Retrieve by relevance and recency, preserve provenance and permissions, and write only useful records with explicit retention.
pitfalls: Agent memory is application-managed state, not the model KV cache.
A stored memory may be stale, unauthorized, or unsupported when recalled.

headings: Memory placement and content type

concepts.title: Reasoning search tree
concepts.meaning: Several partial solution paths are evaluated, pruned, and continued under a budget.
concepts.brief: Compare one linear trace, independent samples with a vote, and a bounded tree search. Show the evaluator and token budget separately from model-generated candidates.
pitfalls: Repeated sampling helps only under assumptions about candidate diversity and aggregation.
A heuristic evaluator can favor fluent but incorrect paths.

headings: Use a problem that actually needs branching

concepts.title: Sandbox execution boundary
concepts.meaning: Generated code runs inside a bounded workspace separated from secrets and network paths.
concepts.brief: Keep generated code, sandbox, and trusted evaluation in distinct zones. Animate filesystem and egress gates plus CPU, memory, and time limits.
pitfalls: A sandbox limits authority but does not make untrusted code harmless.
The trusted supervisor and grading secrets stay outside the worker boundary.

headings: Keep the worker away from the authority to grade it

concepts.title: GUI observe act loop
concepts.meaning: A screen observation grounds a click, then the updated screen confirms the result.
concepts.brief: Alternate observation, target grounding, host authorization, action dispatch, and new-state verification. Keep the agent proposal distinct from the host decision.
pitfalls: A screenshot or accessibility label can be stale or ambiguous.
A typed schema does not guarantee correct target grounding.

headings: The observe-act loop

concepts.title: Tool protocol messages
concepts.meaning: A host and server exchange correlated request and response messages through a client.
concepts.brief: Trace discovery and a request/response exchange across host, client, and server. Keep request IDs, transport, tool errors, and protocol errors distinct.
pitfalls: Request IDs correlate messages; they do not identify conversation memory.
Protocol compatibility does not grant authorization to server capabilities.

headings: Trace the wire before hiding it behind an SDK

concepts.title: Query expansion paths
concepts.meaning: One question becomes several focused retrieval paths whose results are combined.
concepts.brief: Create a standalone rewrite, vocabulary variants, decomposed plan, or hypothetical answer embedding from one question. Retrieve and fuse results while tracking evidence coverage.
pitfalls: HyDE embeds a generated passage; it does not certify that text as evidence.
Decomposition can improve coverage while adding retrieval and synthesis cost.

headings: Query rewriting and decomposition
How HyDE works
Agentic and iterative retrieval

concepts.title: Document segmentation
concepts.meaning: A structured document becomes overlapping and section-aligned retrieval chunks.
concepts.brief: Compare fixed token windows, recursive separators, and structure-aware parent-child chunks. Measure answer completeness and citation spans at actual split boundaries.
pitfalls: Overlap repeats boundary text but cannot recover a missing condition.
Judge chunk boundaries against answerability and citation needs.

headings: Fixed windows show the boundary failure

concepts.title: Evidence retrieval pipeline
concepts.meaning: Versioned source evidence passes access filtering and ranking before it supports an answer.
concepts.brief: Attach source identity, version, and location to chunks. Filter by caller permissions before ranking, pack cited evidence, and abstain when passages do not resolve the answer.
pitfalls: Authorization must run before evidence reaches generation.
A citation points to a span; it does not prove the span supports the claim.

headings: Build the evidence record
Pack evidence for a grounded answer

concepts.title: Training step loop
concepts.meaning: A minibatch cycles through forward, loss, backward, and parameter update.
concepts.brief: Track a minibatch through logits, loss, gradient accumulation, parameter update, and validation. Keep gradient clearing, backward, and optimizer step ordering visible.
pitfalls: Accumulated gradients remain until cleared.
Falling training loss alone does not establish generalization.

headings: The five execution phases in a training step

concepts.title: Response token mask
concepts.meaning: Prompt tokens remain contextual input while selected response tokens receive training loss.
concepts.brief: Serialize a message with its model template, shift input tokens into next-token targets, and distinguish prompt context from assistant targets included in loss.
pitfalls: Masking prompt targets does not remove prompt tokens from contextual attention.
Target shifts and segment-start rules must align with the actual template.

headings: Which tokens should receive the loss?

concepts.title: Prompt search loop
concepts.meaning: Prompt candidates are scored on validation examples and then checked against a separate holdout.
concepts.brief: Generate candidate instructions from training examples, score them against an explicit validation metric, and preserve a separate holdout for final evaluation.
pitfalls: An optimizer can exploit a flawed metric.
Tuning on holdout examples leaks evaluation feedback into prompt selection.

headings: Search instructions as well as demonstrations

concepts.title: Active learning frontier
concepts.meaning: Uncertain examples near a model boundary are selected for human labeling.
concepts.brief: Plot unlabeled cases near a decision boundary, select a subset with an explicit acquisition rule, route it to annotation, then update and independently evaluate.
pitfalls: Uncertainty sampling can over-select noisy or out-of-distribution examples.
Reviewer data and final holdout labels need separate access controls.

headings: Select cases that might teach something new

concepts.title: Fairness matched pairs
concepts.meaning: Equivalent cases travel in parallel while one controlled attribute changes.
concepts.brief: Construct matched examples with one declared wording or identity change. Compare scores, decisions, and subgroup errors under the same task contract and data snapshot.
pitfalls: A matched-pair test supports a narrow behavioral comparison, not a universal fairness claim.
Preserve decision-relevant facts while changing the audited feature.

headings: Build a matched-pair wording audit

concepts.title: Claim evidence link
concepts.meaning: Answer claims connect to specific source spans, with unsupported claims left unlinked.
concepts.brief: Split an answer into atomic claims and bind each to a source span. Keep support, contradiction, and missing-evidence outcomes separate from broader world factuality.
pitfalls: Text overlap does not establish entailment.
Evidence-supported wording may still be stale or unauthorized for the caller.

headings: Verify each atomic claim

concepts.title: Benchmark evidence gap
concepts.meaning: A polished benchmark score is separated from a distinct production evaluation.
concepts.brief: Trace a score through its dataset, harness, contamination controls, metric, and uncertainty. Compare it with production evaluation for safety, retrieval, latency, and user impact.
pitfalls: Different tasks or harnesses make scores incomparable.
A high aggregate score can hide a critical failure slice.

headings: A score is only meaningful with its contract
Diagnose retrieval and generation separately

concepts.title: CUDA grid block warps
concepts.meaning: A grid contains thread blocks, each divided into groups of execution lanes.
concepts.brief: Move a tensor batch from host to device and map work into a grid of blocks and thread warps. Keep launch overhead and data placement visible for small jobs.
pitfalls: The launch grid describes program work; it does not pin a block to one SM.
Device availability and tensor placement are separate checks.

headings: Eight tokens onto two blocks

concepts.title: Precision scale accumulate
concepts.meaning: Compact operands receive scaling before multiplication and wider-precision accumulation.
concepts.brief: Encode operands on a reduced range and precision grid, apply required scales, then accumulate products at the declared precision. Measure rounding, underflow, and saturation.
pitfalls: Scaling cannot restore values already rounded to zero or saturated.
Format bit widths do not specify an entire kernel arithmetic path.

headings: Format taxonomy: range, spacing, and bitfields
Scale ownership and the GEMM dataflow
